commits.message:
fix(taxonomy): cross-process cache staleness was silently re-queuing already-approved terms

hermes-api and hermes-graph-consumer are two separate OS processes,
each with its own independent in-memory cache (a plain @lru_cache is
per-process by construction). Approving a taxonomy candidate only ever
called clear_taxonomy_cache() in the process handling that HTTP
request -- always hermes-api, since that's what serves the review UI.
hermes-graph-consumer -- the process that actually parses live incoming
mail -- kept serving its own stale copy of canonical_skills.json/
job_titles.json for its entire uptime. A term approved through the
review UI could get flagged as "unknown" again by the very next real
email that mentioned it, silently re-queuing work a human had just
finished -- duplicate review effort that only gets worse the longer a
process stays up.

Replaced the plain @lru_cache on load_skills_taxonomy/
load_canonical_skills_taxonomy/load_job_titles_taxonomy (app/
understanding/taxonomy/loader.py) with a cache keyed on the file's own
mtime (_load_json_cached_by_mtime) -- any process, on its own next
read, notices the file changed (written by ANY process, since both
read the same file on the shared runtime volume) and reloads. No
cross-process messaging needed, just a stat() call. build_skill_alias_
index/build_title_alias_index are now deliberately uncached -- they're
built from the (mtime-checked) load functions, and rebuilding the
dict is microseconds over a few hundred entries, not worth a second
caching layer with its own invalidation story. clear_taxonomy_cache()
still explicitly evicts this process's own mtime-cache entry
immediately after a local write, on top of the mtime check already
covering every other process (including this one's own future reads)
-- belt and suspenders against filesystem mtime-resolution granularity.

Deterministic throughout: no LLM, no polling, no new network calls --
a stat() syscall on a file every process already reads directly.

New coverage: a process with an already-warm cache, given a file
change it never triggered itself (standing in for a different process's
write) and no clear_taxonomy_cache() call of its own, still picks up
the change on its next read. Full regression suite (18 checks) green
against a fresh schema and rebuilt image.
